summary.headline: About a third of your MQLs have no consent on record, suppressed leads are still marked active, and 'MQL' means something broader to marketing than to sales — fix all three before an AI touches this list.
summary.narrative: Of 6 MQL-flagged leads, 5 carry 'Unknown' or 'No record' consent — roughly a third of marketable records have no lawful basis. Two suppressed leads (Unsubscribed, Bounced) are still flagged MQL, and cold-list leads have no consent at all. Marketing's MQL definition is also broader than sales' 'Qualified', so the same lead means different things to each team. Re-permission consent, suppress at source, and govern one MQL definition before enabling any AI targeting.

findings.title: About a third of MQLs have no consent on record
findings.what_we_found: Of 6 MQL-flagged leads, 5 carry consent_status 'Unknown' or 'No record' (LD-4005, LD-4008, LD-4010, LD-4014, plus LD-4002 at lead stage) — roughly a third of marketable records have no lawful basis recorded.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: An AI that segments or messages this list would target records with no provable consent, turning a data gap into a compliance and deliverability incident at machine speed.
the_fix: Exclude every 'Unknown'/'No record' consent lead from any AI-targetable segment until a lawful basis is on file.
Run a re-permission / preference-confirmation pass to backfill consent where possible.
Make consent_status a required, validated field at lead capture.
findings.evidence: consent_status = 'Unknown' or 'No record' on 5 of 6 MQL-flagged leads.

findings.title: Suppressed leads still flagged as active MQLs
findings.what_we_found: LD-4008 (Unsubscribed) and LD-4010 (Bounced) are still flagged mql_flag = Yes and would be picked up by any active-audience query.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: An AI building an audience from active MQLs would re-message people who opted out or whose address bounced, damaging deliverability and breaching their stated preference.
the_fix: Suppress Unsubscribed and Bounced records at the source so they cannot enter a marketable audience.
Add a guard that excludes any non-Subscribed subscription_status from MQL/active segments.
Reconcile mql_flag against subscription_status on a schedule.

findings.title: Cold-list leads carry no consent
findings.what_we_found: LD-4011 and LD-4014 originate from a 'Cold list' source with consent_status 'No record'.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Cold, unconsented leads are out of scope for any AI messaging step; an AI that includes them would message people with no relationship or lawful basis. Align with the org-wide roadmap on cold-list scope.
the_fix: Quarantine all cold-list, unconsented leads from AI-targetable segments.
Establish a lawful basis (explicit opt-in) before any outreach.
Flag cold-list scope to the org-wide roadmap so the boundary is governed centrally.

findings.title: Marketing's MQL definition is broader than sales' Qualified
findings.what_we_found: Marketing flags an MQL on a score threshold OR a content download, regardless of budget or authority — broader than sales' 'Qualified' (budget confirmed AND economic buyer identified).
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: The same lead means different things to each team; an AI routing or scoring on 'MQL' would hand sales records they do not consider qualified, breaking the handoff.
the_fix: Convene marketing and sales to agree one canonical, governed MQL/Qualified definition.
Encode the shared definition in both systems before any AI routes or scores a lead.
Submit both definitions to the semantic-reconciler to confirm the conflict is resolved.
findings.evidence: Marketing MQL = score OR content download; sales Qualified = budget AND economic buyer.

definitions.definition: MQL = a lead whose score is above the marketing threshold OR who completed a content download, regardless of budget or authority.
definitions.derived_from: leads.csv mql_flag column and lifecycle_stage = 'MQL' rows
